set.st: George A. Smalley, a former McBain resident accused in a Chicago & West Michigan train robbery and a shooting near Grand Rapids, got off the train at McBain and was shot dead by a sheriff's posse in Aug 1895. No money was found on him. Smalley was shot about 8 pm on 24 Aug 1895 in the doorway of a one-room shanty with a rear lean-to in McBain, where the woman he called his wife lived with her mother; the shooters were Gillis McBain and Deputy Spafford of Cadillac. He had 30 cents on him, and his bundle left at Stewart's saloon held only a shirt. Neither 1895 paper mentions any hidden loot. Later treasure write-ups say the loot was hidden near Farwell or McBain. A gang member's 1895 confession: the loot came from an 1893 Indiana express robbery; his share was spent on property at McBain and about $2,700 plus jewellery was recovered there. Only papers were said to be buried, in Indiana. No Michigan cache.
set.t: The loot claim exists only in a modern write-up; the 1895 papers describe a penniless man. Record only unless a period paper names a cache.
